lesson.title: 911 – Procedure 104: Event Creation Codes (10-01 to 10-09)
objectives: Identify and explain the purpose of each event-creation code from 10-01 through 10-09.
Apply the specific usage rules and restrictions for each event-creation code.
Differentiate between codes that instruct units to contact their command, the dispatcher, or verify location.
Recognize that 10-08 and 10-09 are not used, as specified in Procedure 104.

questions.stem: According to Procedure 104, what does radio code 10-01 mean?

choices.text: REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND
CALL YOUR COMMAND
CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE
VERIFY ADDRESS

questions.solution: Procedure 104 lists 10-01 as CALL YOUR COMMAND, and notes that the message should NOT come over the dispatcher’s air from the command.

questions.stem: For code 10-01 CALL YOUR COMMAND, Procedure 104 states that this message should NOT come over the dispatcher’s air from the command.
Code 10-01 is defined as “CALL YOUR __________,” and the guide notes that this message should not come over the dispatcher’s air from the command.
Match each detail to code 10-01 CALL YOUR COMMAND.
answer: Who is the unit instructed to contact?
Their command
Should the command’s message be transmitted over the dispatcher’s air?
No, it should NOT come over the dispatcher’s air.
Is 10-01 an event creation code or a final disposition?
Event creation code
Under which Procedure is 10-01 defined?
Procedure 104 – Radio Code Signals

questions.stem: What instruction does code 10-02 give to the unit?

choices.text: CALL YOUR COMMAND
REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND
STAND BY
CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE

questions.solution: 10-02 is REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND, and the guide adds instructions about completing assignments first unless it is an emergency.

questions.stem: For code 10-02, Procedure 104 states that unless it is an emergency, units should be advised to complete their assignments before responding to their command.
Code 10-02 is REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND, and the guide says that unless it is an __________, units will be advised to complete their assignments before responding.
Match each statement with how it applies to code 10-02 REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND.
answer: Base instruction to the unit
Report to your command
What should the unit do with their current assignment if it is not an emergency?
Complete the assignment before responding.
Is this primarily about radio contact or physical reporting?
Physical reporting to the command
Is 10-02 an event creation or out-of-service code?
Event creation code

questions.stem: What does radio code 10-03 instruct the unit to do?

choices.text: Call their command
Call the dispatcher by telephone
Report to their command in person
Verify the address with the complainant

questions.solution: Procedure 104 defines 10-03 as CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE and instructs that if the number is unknown, it should be transmitted at the same time.

questions.stem: For code 10-03 CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE, the dispatcher must transmit the telephone number to be used if it is unknown to the unit.
When using code 10-03 CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE, if the phone number is unknown, the dispatcher should transmit the __________ to be used at the same time.
Match each aspect of code 10-03 CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE with the correct detail.
answer: Who the unit is instructed to call
The dispatcher
What additional information must be transmitted if unknown
The telephone number to be used
Is 10-03 an event creation code or an out-of-service code?
Event creation code
Which procedure defines this requirement?
Procedure 104 – Radio Code Signals

questions.stem: What is the correct use of code 10-04, according to Procedure 104?

choices.text: To request a repeat of a message that was not heard
To acknowledge a transmission that was heard and understood
To verify a unit’s current address
To place a unit out of service for mechanical issues

questions.solution: 10-04 is ACKNOWLEDGMENT and should NOT be used if a transmission was not heard or understood.

questions.stem: Code 10-04 ACKNOWLEDGMENT should be used when a transmission was not heard or understood.
Procedure 104 says that 10-04 ACKNOWLEDGMENT should NOT be used if a transmission was not __________ or understood.
Match each statement to how it relates to 10-04 ACKNOWLEDGMENT.
answer: Primary purpose of 10-04
To acknowledge a transmission that was heard and understood.
Should 10-04 be used when the message was not heard?
No, it should NOT be used in that case.
If the dispatcher did not understand a unit, what code should be used instead?
10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE.
Is 10-04 defined in the event-creation section of Procedure 104?
Yes, it appears with the 10-01 through 10-07 instructions.

questions.stem: When should code 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE be used?

choices.text: When the dispatcher needs the unit to call their command
When a message was not heard or understood
When verifying the unit’s current address
When the unit has arrived on the scene

questions.solution: Procedure 104 states that 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE is to be used when a message was not heard or understood.

questions.stem: Code 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE should be used instead of 10-04 when the dispatcher did not hear or understand the transmission.
Procedure 104 defines 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE as to be used when the message was not __________ or understood.
Match each scenario to whether 10-05 should be used, based on Procedure 104.
answer: Dispatcher clearly heard and understood the unit’s message.
Do NOT use 10-05; 10-04 may be appropriate.
Dispatcher did NOT hear the message due to static.
Use 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE.
Dispatcher heard the unit but did NOT understand what was said.
Use 10-05 REPEAT MESSAGE.
Dispatcher wants the unit to verify their current address.
Do NOT use 10-05; use 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of code 10-06 STAND BY in Procedure 104?

choices.text: To have the unit call their command
To advise units to wait for a message
To report to the precinct station house
To verify the unit’s current location

questions.solution: 10-06 STAND BY is defined as to be used when advising units to wait for a message.

questions.stem: Code 10-06 STAND BY is used when advising units to wait for a message.
Procedure 104 states that 10-06 STAND BY is to be used when advising units to __________ for a message.
Match each dispatcher action with whether 10-06 STAND BY is appropriate.
answer: Dispatcher is about to look up more information and will answer shortly.
Use 10-06 STAND BY.
Dispatcher wants the unit to immediately call the command.
Do NOT use 10-06; use 10-01.
Dispatcher wants the unit to wait while another transmission is completed.
Use 10-06 STAND BY.
Dispatcher needs the unit to verify its current location.
Do NOT use 10-06; use 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS.

questions.stem: According to Procedure 104, when is code 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS used?

choices.text: Whenever a caller’s address needs to be confirmed
Only when a dispatcher wants to know the unit’s current location
When the unit must report to their command
When the dispatcher wants the unit to stand by

questions.solution: 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS is only used when the dispatcher wants to know the unit’s current location.

questions.stem: Code 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS may be used whenever the dispatcher wants to confirm the complainant’s home address.
10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS is only used when a dispatcher wants to know the unit’s current __________.
Match each use case with whether 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS is appropriate.
answer: Dispatcher needs to know where the responding unit is right now.
Use 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS.
Dispatcher needs to confirm the complainant’s callback number.
Do NOT use 10-07; this is not the unit’s location.
Dispatcher wants the unit to check a different address on the job.
10-07 is not for checking a second job address; it is for the unit’s current location.
Dispatcher wants to know the exact intersection where the RMP is stopped.
Use 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS, as it asks for the unit’s current location.

questions.stem: How is code 10-08 defined in Procedure 104?

choices.text: OUT OF SERVICE (MECHANICAL)
ARRIVED AT SCENE
NOT USED
CALL YOUR COMMAND

questions.solution: The 10-08 entry in Procedure 104 is explicitly listed as NOT USED.

questions.stem: Code 10-08 is marked as NOT USED in Procedure 104 and should not be transmitted over the air.
In the event-creation section of Procedure 104, 10-08 is listed simply as __________.
Match each statement to whether it correctly reflects how 10-08 is treated in Procedure 104.
answer: Defined with a specific instruction for units.
Incorrect – 10-08 is listed as NOT USED.
Dispatcher should avoid using this code over the air.
Correct – it is marked NOT USED.
Appears in the same section as 10-01 through 10-07.
Correct – it is part of the event-creation list.
May be activated for pilot projects when unused codes are needed.
Possible – the note in Procedure 104 says unused codes may be activated for pilot projects.

questions.stem: How is code 10-09 defined in Procedure 104?

choices.text: MEAL
PRECINCT ASSIGNMENT
NOT USED
CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE

questions.solution: Procedure 104 lists 10-09 as NOT USED, directly under 10-08 which is also NOT USED.

questions.stem: Like 10-08, code 10-09 is also marked NOT USED in the event-creation section of Procedure 104.
The guide labels 10-09 as __________, indicating there is no active definition for this code.
Match each statement about 10-09 NOT USED to its correctness under Procedure 104.
answer: Dispatcher should create their own meaning for 10-09 if needed.
Incorrect – code is NOT USED and should not be improvised.
10-09 appears in the same block as 10-08, both marked NOT USED.
Correct – both 10-08 and 10-09 are listed as NOT USED.
10-09 currently has no operational instruction in the event-creation section.
Correct – it is simply listed as NOT USED.
Unused codes, like 10-09, may be activated for pilot projects if directed.
Correct – the note in Procedure 104 states that unused codes may be activated for pilot projects.
